key: And the LORD turned towards him, and said: ‘Go in this thy might, and save Israel from the hand of Midian; have not I sent thee?’
s: When Gideon, threshing in hiding, asks where the wonders of the Exodus have gone, he is given his charge; Rashi, on 6:14, with Rabbi Tanchuma, reads ‘this thy might’ as the merit of his having pleaded in Israel’s defence.

evidence.words: פסח היה, אמר לו: אמש הקרני אבא את ההלל, ושמעתיו שהיה אומר (תהלים קיד א): בצאת ישראל ממצרים, 'ועתה נטשנו', אם צדיקים היו אבותינו, יעשה לנו בזכותם, ואם רשעים היו, כשם שעשה להם נפלאותיו חנם כן יעשה לנו, ואיה כל נפלאותיו … בכח הזכות הזה שלמדת סניגוריא על בני, כך דרש רבי תנחומא (מדרש תנחומא שופטים ד)
evidence.gloss: [On 6:13, ‘which our fathers told us of’:] It was Passover. He said to him: last night my father read me the Hallel, and I heard him saying, ‘When Israel came forth out of Egypt’, ‘and now He has cast us off’. If our fathers were righteous, let Him act for us in their merit; and if they were wicked, just as He did His wonders for them freely, so let Him do for us; and where are all His wonders? … [On 6:14, ‘in this thy might’:] In the might of this merit, that you pleaded in defence of My children; so Rabbi Tanchuma expounded (Midrash Tanchuma, Shoftim 4).

reason: verse.js ok, ref Judges 6:14 and at [216,14] match; the key is the whole of 6:14 and ends in ‘?’’. Plain sense faithful: Gideon beats out wheat in the winepress to hide it from Midian (6:11) and asks where the wondrous works of the going out of Egypt are (6:13); 6:14 gives him his charge; no four-word run from the key. Read the whole chapter 6 packet. Rashi on 6:14 (בכחך זה) reads it as the might of the merit of his having pleaded in defence of God’s children, and names it as Rabbi Tanchuma’s exposition; his 6:13 comment gives the plea itself. The sentence names Rabbi Tanchuma only as Rashi’s own stated source, and quotes three words of the key in curly quotes. Metzudat David on 6:14 says the same, and Radak on 6:11 reports the same midrash while on 6:14 he reads the might as strength God clothed him with; Rashi is the default and his words carry the sentence.
